content.title: About
content.content: Plain whole‑milk yogurt is made by fermenting whole cow’s milk with live cultures of Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus. It has a creamy texture, mild milky flavor, and contains about 3.5 % fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt is one of the oldest fermented dairy foods, with evidence of production over 5,000 years ago in Central Asia.
Traditional preparation involves heating milk to 85 °C, cooling to 45 °C, then adding a starter culture.
Live cultures in yogurt can help improve gut microbiota balance.
Plain yogurt is often used as a base for sauces, marinades, and desserts in many cuisines.
Whole‑milk yogurt retains more fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) than low‑fat versions.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Live bacteria support a healthy gut microbiome, which may aid digestion and immune function.

items.title: Calcium and Vitamin D
items.content: Whole milk provides calcium and vitamin D essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Yogurt supplies high‑quality milk protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and cobalamin (B12), important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Fatty Acids
items.content: The fat in whole milk includes conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), studied for potential anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: Higher fat content
items.content: Whole‑milk yogurt is higher in calories and saturated fat; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Added sugars in some brands
items.content: While plain yogurt is typically unsweetened, some manufacturers add sugar; check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy yogurt as a snack, blend into smoothies, use as a base for dressings, sauces, desserts, or top with fruit, honey, and nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store yogurt in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
